fixes.explanation: Close, but Abram turns the offer down. The king of Sodom says, "Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself." Abram answers that he has raised his hand to the LORD God Most High, and he won't accept even a thread or a strap of a sandal (Gen 14:21-23). I think that's a man with a clear head. Plenty of us can't pass up a free sample, and he's walking away from a whole pile of goods.

False is right, baker. The king of Sodom says, "take the goods for yourself," but Abram refuses to accept even a thread or a strap of a sandal. He declares that he has raised his hand to the LORD God Most High, so that the king can't say, "I have made Abram rich" (Gen 14:21-23). That man said no to a mountain of goods. Meanwhile I get nervous leaving the last cookie on the plate.

True, baker! Abram tells the king he will accept nothing except what his men have eaten and the share for the men who went with him. Then he names Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, and says they may take their portion (Gen 14:24). He doesn't force their hand either way. He only says that the share is theirs to take, and the text doesn't say what they did.

Not quite, friend. Abram says he will accept nothing except what his men have eaten and the share for the men who went with him. Then he says of Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, "They may take their portion" (Gen 14:24). So the verse says what the card says, and True is the right answer. Abram keeps nothing for himself, but he doesn't speak for their shares.
